title: Isolate IO strand and introduce adaptive lease throttle to reduce batcher stalls
creator: Ethan Zhang
description:
Problem:
Under sustained high-concurrency workloads we observe intermittent batcher stalls and KV cache thrashing when the scheduler tries to reclaim memory or evict hot sessions. Root cause analysis points to three correlated issues:
 1) IO and mmap work (session persistence and KV snapshotting) are executed on the batcher/controller threads, causing head-of-line blocking for latency-sensitive lanes.
 2) The lease/heartbeat protocol that coordinates slot ownership and KV priming is conservative and amplifies contention under memory pressure, resulting in stalled batching pipelines.
 3) Legacy session serialization uses multiple copies and locks, increasing alloc pressure and causing jitter in the scheduler's admission window.

Goal:
- Separate the IO/mmap/compaction pathway from the continuous-batching control plane (introduce an isolated IO strand).
- Implement an adaptive lease-throttle that reduces lease churn under memory pressure instead of immediate aggressive evictions.
- Replace the session serializer with a zero-copy, versioned buffer format to reduce allocations and lock contention.
- Upgrade jemalloc to 5.3.0 and libcgroup bindings to latest stable to reduce fragmentation and improve reclaim behavior.

Approach/Design decisions:
- Isolated IO strand: spawn a bounded worker pool responsible for all disk and mmap operations. Batch controller enqueues persistence jobs with backpressure signals; critical-path token flows remain lock-free and unaffected by IO latency. This is intentionally a per-shard pool to preserve NUMA locality.
- Adaptive lease-throttle: compute a soft lease-renew probability based on the shard's free memory ratio and recent eviction rate. During pressure, throttle renewals and extend grace windows for active sessions that show steady token consumption to avoid flapping.
- Session serializer: adopt a compact, TLV-like on-wire layout with an object table for repeated tensors and a small header for versioning. Use platform-provided iovec scatter-gather for zero-copy writes where supported. Fallback path keeps compatibility with older snapshots and performs a one-time migration.
- Dependency upgrades: bump jemalloc and libcgroup; ensure CI stress lanes exercise malloc hooks and oom behavior. Add a migration tool for on-disk session snapshots.

Tradeoffs and risks:
- Introducing the IO strand reduces tail latency but adds complexity in error propagation and job cancellation. We'll need robust cancellation semantics to avoid leaking work when shards are drained.
- Adaptive lease behavior can mask real memory pressure if thresholds set too lax; risk of OOM if throttling prevents necessary evictions. We'll add conservative safeties and an emergency fast-evict path tied to node OOM signals.
- Snapshot migration increases maintenance (two code paths) but limited to first run after rollout and can be gated via a feature flag.
acceptance_criteria: No regression in steady-state throughput (<= 3% variance).
P99 tail latency for generation requests reduced by at least 30% under synthetic mixed workload that previously caused stalls.
Observed lease churn (renewals/sec) reduced by >= 45% during induced memory-pressure tests without increasing eviction rate beyond baseline emergency threshold.
CI stress test (72h churn test) shows no batcher deadlocks and <0.1% request failures attributable to scheduler races.
On-disk snapshot migration completes successfully on a node with 10k sessions; migration time tracked and logged.
Rollout playbook documented and validated in a staging cluster; feature flags exist to disable new behaviors quickly.
comments: 2026-01-29 - Ethan Zhang: Posted initial RCA after reproducer run with 50 clients and synthetic long-lived sessions. Attached flame graphs and heap profiles to attachments.

2026-02-05 - Priya Kapoor: Spike completed for isolated IO strand. Measured tail latency improvement in microbench: p99 down from 420ms -> 260ms on a 16-GPU host under mixed workload. Pushed branch eng/isolated-io-spike for early review.
2026-02-18 - Systems Team (review): Recommended per-NUMA pool to avoid cross-node memory pressure. Also suggested integrating with existing slot prewarmer to avoid IO storms during scale-up.
2026-02-24 - Security Review: No data exfiltration concerns. Ensure migration tool honors snapshot encryption keys; flagged for follow-up integration test.
2026-03-02 - Priya Kapoor: Adaptive lease-throttle prototype merged to feature branch. Added metrics: lease_renew_rate, lease_throttle_factor, eviction_wave_count.

2026-03-08 - Performance: Full stress bench (1000 sessions hot, 10k cold) shows average throughput +18% and reduced allocator churn. Noted a minor memory leak in fallback serializer path; created follow-up ENG-552000.
2026-03-10 - Priya Kapoor: Preparing canary rollout plan. Staged on eu-west-1, 2 shards behind a feature flag. Need on-call assignment and rollback checklist.
notes: Follow-up tickets: ENH-assign-oncall-for-canary (created by SRE), ENG-552000 (fix fallback serializer leak).
Rollout strategy: start with non-customer-critical shards; observe lease_renew_rate and eviction_wave_count for 48h before wider rollout.
Ops runbook must include: how to flip snapshot migration off, how to disable IO strand pool, and how to force immediate evictions in emergency.
Perf tracking: add a synthetic workload job in Jenkins/cron that runs nightly and posts P95/P99 to the release dashboard.
If migration hits incompatibilities, fallback plan: continue serving with legacy serializer for the shard and schedule a dedicated maintenance window to run offline migration tooling.
